root.name: Bogo-Indian Defense: Grünfeld Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 Bb4+ 4. Nbd2

overview: White develops the knight to d2 with 4.Nbd2, avoiding the doubled pawns of 4.Nc3 and 4.Bd2 trades. Black chooses between ...O-O, ...d5 and ...b6, usually reaching a QGD-style or Queen's Indian set-up. White plays a3 and e3 with Qc2 and an e4 break. The game is quiet and strategic.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with a3 to ask the bishop, then e3 and Qc2

black_ideas.idea: Trade the bishop on d2 or retreat to e7
Aim for equality in a QGD structure

typical_structures.structure: QGD-style centre with c4/d4 v d5/e6

character.notes: Quiet and positional, a low-risk line for both sides.

structure.notes: Centre tension between c4/d4 and e6/d5, flexible.

approach.notes: A regular choice for strong players among Bogo-Indian lines.

level.notes: No concrete lines but careful positional play.
